Definition: from G1537 and G906; to eject (literally or figuratively):--bring forth, cast (forth, out), drive (out), expel, leave, pluck (pull, take, thrust) out, put forth (out), send away (forth, out).
BiblicalUsage: To cast out is to throw out with force, and the Gospels use it for demons, for buyers in the temple, and for the lost. Jesus casts out devils by the Spirit of God, preaches in the synagogues and casts out devils, and promises that whoever comes to Him He will in no wise cast out. The same force that drives out evil welcomes in the sinner, and that is the whole gospel in one word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus casts out demons but never casts out sinners, because His power drives away what harms us and His mercy keeps what comes to Him. I hold that no one who comes to Him will be turned away, and that includes me.
